title: 25+ Under Sink Organizer Ideas for a Tidy 2026
excerpt: Discover 25+ under sink organizer ideas for your kitchen and bathroom. Practical tips, product picks, and space-saving solutions for 2026.
content: Have you ever opened the cabinet under your kitchen or bathroom sink, then shut it right back because of the chaos inside? You are not alone. The space under the sink is one of the most overlooked corners of the home, even though its storage potential is huge. This is where the right **under sink organizer ideas** can turn that dark, cramped space into a tidy, functional, easy-to-reach storage zone. This article rounds up more than 25 creative ideas you can put to work at home in 2026, for both the kitchen and the bathroom.
![Under sink organizer ideas with pull-out drawers and wire baskets in a modern kitchen](/images/blog/under-sink-organizer-ideas-hero.webp)
## Why Does the Under-Sink Area Get So Messy?
Before we get to the solutions, it helps to understand the root of the problem. The space under the sink has a few unique challenges that make it hard to organize without the right strategy.
### The Main Challenges of Under-Sink Space
• **Pipes in the way** running through the middle of the cabinet, so a standard shelf cannot use the space fully
• **High humidity** that makes items damp, and even moldy if you are not careful
• **A narrow door** that makes items in the back hard to reach
• **No built-in dividers**, so everything gets jumbled together
• **Items of all sizes**, from tall soap bottles and small buckets to plastic bags that have no fixed home

According to [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com), a leading home organization outlet, the under-sink area is one of the most common clutter hot spots in the home because it lacks a structured storage system. With the right system, this space can become one of the most efficient storage areas in your house.

## 25+ Best Under Sink Organizer Ideas for Kitchen and Bathroom
The ideas below are grouped by product type and organizing method so you can pick whichever fits your space and needs best.
### 1. Pull-Out Drawer Organizer

The pull-out drawer is the number one solution for under-sink space. It mounts inside the cabinet and slides forward so even the items in the very back are easy to reach. Available in wire or plastic, prices range from about $15 to $45 depending on size and material.
### 2. Tension Rod for Spray Bottles

A tension rod is a no-drill support bar installed horizontally inside the cabinet. Hang spray cleaner bottles from the rod by their triggers so the cabinet floor stays clear and every bottle is easy to see. This is one of the most budget-friendly **under sink organizer ideas** because tension rods are so cheap.
### 3. Lazy Susan (Turntable)

A lazy Susan is a round tray that spins a full 360 degrees. Set one in the corner under the sink to hold soap bottles, cleaning liquids, or care products. Give it a spin and you can reach items in the back without digging through the whole cabinet. Quality plastic lazy Susans start around $10.
![Under sink bathroom organizer with stackable bins and pull-out rack for toiletries](/images/blog/under-sink-organizer-ideas-section-1.webp)
### 4. Stackable Clear Bins

Stackable clear storage bins are a classic that never fails. Choose different sizes for different items: large bins for sponges and rags, medium bins for cleaning products, and small bins for little things like rubber bands or spare bottle caps. The clear sides let you see the contents without opening each one.
### 5. Over-the-Door Organizer

The inside of the cabinet door often gets overlooked. Hang a plastic or fabric organizer on the inside of the door to store rubber gloves, small brushes, or other thin products. It is a smart way to use hidden vertical space.
### 6. Wire Baskets With Labels

Medium wire baskets are perfect for grouping by category: one basket for floor cleaners, one for kitchen products, one for sink care. Add a label to each basket so everyone in the household knows where to put things back after use. ### 7. Two-Tier Shelf

A two-tier shelf is designed to use the height of the under-sink space, which is usually tall but underused. Put frequently used items on the lower tier and backup stock on the upper tier. Make sure the shelf you choose can work around the pipes.
### 8. Hanging Storage Pockets

Fabric or plastic pockets that hang on the door hinge or cabinet wall are perfect for lightweight items. This is especially handy under the bathroom sink for storing beauty products, a spare comb, or wet wipes.
### 9. A Plastic Bag Holder
In most kitchens, plastic bags pile up in large numbers. Use a cylinder or rectangular dispenser mounted on the inside cabinet wall to store and pull out plastic bags neatly and in order.
![Creative under kitchen sink organizer idea using tension rod and lazy susan turntable](/images/blog/under-sink-organizer-ideas-section-2.webp)
### 10. A Waterproof Liner for the Cabinet Base

Before placing any organizer, lay a waterproof mat or liner on the base of the under-sink cabinet. This protects the cabinet floor from water drips and makes cleanup easier. These liners come in various sizes and can be cut to fit.
### 11. A Mini Pegboard on the Cabinet Wall

Install a small pegboard on the inside side wall of the cabinet to hang accessories like brushes, rags, or gloves. This is a technique often recommended by [Houzz](https://www.houzz.com), a leading interior design and home renovation platform, for making the most of vertical space that usually gets ignored.
### 12. Dedicated Bins for Kitchen Products

Under the kitchen sink specifically, separate storage areas by function: a zone for cleaning products, a zone for bags and plastic wrap, a zone for sponges and brushes, and a zone for backup supplies. This zoning system prevents everything from mixing together and makes grabbing what you need much faster.
### 13. Small Containers for Batteries and Odds and Ends
If you store little things like spare batteries, matches, or rubber bands under the sink, use small lidded, labeled containers. This keeps small items from scattering and getting lost.
### 14. A Pipe-Friendly Organizer
This product is designed with a notch or gap in the middle to accommodate the pipes. Invest in this type if your pipes sit in the center of the cabinet, since a regular organizer will not fit well.
### 15. An Adjustable Shelf

A shelf with movable supports lets you adjust the height for bottles of different sizes. Today you might store a tall disinfectant bottle, tomorrow a small bottle of dish soap. That flexibility is invaluable.

## Under Sink Organizer Ideas Just for the Kitchen

The space under the kitchen sink has different needs than the bathroom. This is usually where you keep chemical cleaners, sponges, kitchen towels, plastic bags, and sometimes backup kitchen tools. Here are ideas designed specifically for the kitchen context.
### 16. A Three-Zone System for the Kitchen
Divide the under-sink kitchen space into three main zones:
1. **Active zone** at the very front for daily items like dish soap and sponges
2. **Stock zone** in the middle for unopened backup products
3. **Rarely used zone** at the very back for occasional items like oven cleaner or drain unclogger
### 17. A Hidden Mini Trash Can

Many homes use the space under the kitchen sink to keep a small trash can. This is practical as long as the can has a snug lid and is lined with a bag to prevent odors. Place it on the side where it does not block access to other items.
### 18. A Vertical Bottle Holder

Instead of laying detergent or dish soap bottles down or stacking them haphazardly, use a dedicated holder that keeps bottles standing upright side by side. This saves floor space and makes them easy to grab.
### 19. Magnetic Strips for Small Tools

Mount a thin magnetic strip on the inside cabinet wall to hang small metal kitchen tools like a scraper or a small metal spoon that usually lives under the sink. It is a clever trick that rarely comes to mind.
### 20. Separate Recycling Bins

If your household is embracing a more eco-friendly lifestyle, you can place two small bins under the kitchen sink: one for organic waste and one for recycling. This fits right in with the [sustainable living](https://www.sesoris.com/blog/living-sustainable-life-eco-friendly-home-organization-ideas-2026) trend that keeps gaining popularity in 2026.
## Under Sink Organizer Ideas Just for the Bathroom

The space under the bathroom sink tends to hold personal care products, light medications, and cleaning supplies. Bathroom humidity is usually higher than in the kitchen, so your choice of organizer material matters a lot.
### 21. A Lidded Medicine Box
Separate light medications (bandages, wound ointment, vitamins) into a tightly lidded plastic box and label it clearly. Make sure it is kept out of reach of children if you have little ones at home.
### 22. A Hair Care Product Organizer

Hair dryers, combs, and various hair accessories often end up scattered under the bathroom sink. Use a tall cylinder or long box to store the hair dryer upright, and a separate small basket for hair accessories.
### 23. A Portable Shower Caddy

A shower caddy is a basket or tray with a handle that you can move around. Fill it with the products you often bring into the shower: soap, shampoo, conditioner, and more. When it is not in use, just tuck it under the sink.
### 24. Storage for Tissues and Cleaning Supplies
Store your stock of toilet paper, wet wipes, and other cleaning supplies in a labeled clear box under the bathroom sink. This makes it easy to see when supplies are running low and need a refill.
![Before and after under sink cabinet organization transformation with bins and pull-out rack](/images/blog/under-sink-organizer-ideas-section-4.webp)
### 25. A Diffuser and Aromatherapy Products
If you keep a diffuser or essential oils in the bathroom, set up a dedicated zone under the sink with a spill-proof liner. This keeps your scented products organized and protected.
## Tips for Choosing the Right Under-Sink Organizer
With so many options out there, choosing the right organizer can feel confusing. Here is a quick guide to use as a reference before you shop.
> Measure first, buy second. This is the single most important rule when choosing an organizer for the under-sink space.
### Recommended Materials
• **PP plastic (polypropylene)** is moisture resistant, lightweight, and easy to clean, great for the bathroom
• **Epoxy-coated wire** is strong with good airflow, great for the kitchen
• **Bamboo** is attractive and eco-friendly, but needs extra care in damp areas
• **Clear acrylic** makes contents easy to see, but is more prone to cracking under a hard impact
### What to Measure Before You Buy
1. Measure the overall interior width, depth, and height of the cabinet
2. Measure the diameter and position of the pipes inside the cabinet
3. Measure the distance from the pipes to the side wall of the cabinet
4. Measure the cabinet door height for over-the-door organizers

## How to Start Organizing Under the Sink
Once you have the inspiration and the right products, it is time to start organizing. Here are the steps I recommend:
1. **Empty the entire cabinet** and set everything out on the floor or a table
2. **Sort and toss** anything expired, broken, or no longer used
3. **Group items** by category or how often you use them
4. **Clean the inside of the cabinet**, including the walls and floor, then lay a waterproof liner
5. **Install the organizers**, starting with the ones that mount on the wall or door, then the ones that sit on the floor
6. **Load in your items** by the groups you set up
7. **Add labels** to each box or zone so everyone in the household understands the system

## FAQ: Common Questions About Under-Sink Organizers
**Q: How do I organize under the sink if there is a big pipe in the middle?**

Choose an organizer designed to accommodate pipes, like a U-shaped pull-out drawer or two separate drawers placed on the left and right of the pipe. You can also use shorter pull-out drawers and use the space above the pipe with a lazy Susan or a flat tray.
**Q: Which material lasts longest for an under-sink organizer in the bathroom?**

PP plastic (polypropylene) and epoxy- or chrome-coated wire are the best choices for damp environments. Avoid untreated wood, since it is prone to moisture damage. For the bathroom, choose materials that do not rust and wipe clean easily.
**Q: How often should the under-sink area be cleaned and reorganized?**

Ideally, do a quick check every month to make sure there are no small leaks and everything is still in its place. Do a deep clean and review the cabinet contents every three months, or at least twice a year.
**Q: Is it safe to store chemical cleaners under the sink?**

It is safe as long as products are kept in their original, tightly sealed containers and out of reach of children. Make sure the cabinet is well ventilated and there is no risk of spills that could damage the cabinet material. Never mix different chemical cleaners in one container.
**Q: How do I keep the under-sink cabinet smelling fresh?**

Place a cabinet freshener sachet or a few scented liner sheets in the corner of the cabinet. Make sure there are no water leaks and the cabinet stays dry. You can also use a small container of baking soda to absorb odors naturally.
